text:
site-bot: ALERT /prod/serving latency spike: p95 > 1200ms for 5m on route /v1/generate :rotating_light:

lena (oncall): I'm on it, paging SRE. can someone grab metrics + recent deploys?

omar: grabbing traces and kv cache dashboard now. seeing sustained growth in kv_cache_entries across pods.

kevin: i see a recent config rollout 03:12 that bumped continuous_batch.max_size from 16 -> 64 and enabled aggressive kv-warmup. rollouts: #6447.

maria: timeline matches. when batch size jumped we started getting larger per-request prefix caches, memory pressure up.

lena (oncall): possible cache-amplification -> GC + tail latency. is autoscaler thrashing?

omar: yes HPA shows ups downs, minReplicas 2, targetCPU 55%. pods spinning 2->6->2 in ~3m windows. warmup is delaying steady-state so cache misses spike on new pods -> drive more load.

kevin: this is a feedback loop: larger batch size => more kv entries per request => new pod warmup slow => increased latency => more inflight requests => HPA scales -> new pods start cold -> miss -> more latency.

dmitri: confirmed error spikes for customers A and B (timeouts 504s). impact: 3% of traffic, 12% of enterprise requests, some customers hitting retry storms.

lena (oncall): set priority: 1) stop the loop 2) reduce customer impact 3) remediate root cause. suggestions?

maria: quick mitigation: revert batch-size change or toggle feature-flag to cap batch to 16. rollback is heavier. toggling flag is fastest.

kevin: also can tune HPA to avoid thrash: set minReplicas=3, increase stabilizationWindowSeconds to 180, and set cooldown to reduce aggressive scale-down. but patching HPA takes a bit.

lena (oncall): do both in parallel. kevin patch HPA. maria flip flag. omar watch dashboards. dmitri communicate to CS.

kevin: running patch now:

```
kubectl patch hpa serving-runtime -n prod --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":3,"behavior":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":180}}}}'
```

kevin: patch applied. HPA now minReplicas=3 and scaleDown stabilization=180s.

maria: toggling FF: continuous_batch.max_size_cap -> 16 for prod via config service. command:

```
POST https://config.prod.internal/flags/toggle
{
  "flag": "continuous_batch.max_size_cap",
  "value": 16,
  "env": "prod"
}
```

maria: flag flip acknowledged. new requests should obey 16 cap within ~30s.

omar: dashboards: p95 dropped from 1350ms -> 420ms within 2 minutes after flag flip. kv_cache_entries rate dropping.

dmitri: incident impact note: customers A/B still seeing intermittent 504s but error rate down 70%. CS notified and we suggested retry with backoff.

lena (oncall): nice. follow-ups: - create rollback PR for the batch change + add staged rollout plan - add automatic HPA cooldown on batch-related rollouts - add cache size alert and a runbook step to cap batch size

kevin: opened PR #6651 to add staged rollout and automated canary checks for kv growth.

maria: filed ticket INC-2487: "cache amplification from continuous batching" with root-cause notes and recommended fixes.

lena (oncall): handoff time. current state: mitigations in place (flag cap, HPA tuned), p95 ~ 400ms, error rate ~0.6% (was 2.1%). assign follow-ups to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

dmitri: i'll stay for 15m to help with customer follow-ups, then hand to oncall.

sre-rotation-bot: @team oncall rotation: next oncall is kevin in 15 minutes.

kevin: I'll take over after dmitri. will keep watching logs and work on PR review.

lena (oncall): thanks everyone. doc the runbook tweak: add explicit step to "cap batch size via feature flag" and checklist to bump HPA minReplicas when enabling larger batches.

omar: pasting quick runbook snippet:

```
Runbook extract - KV cache/batching regression
1) Check kv_cache_entries and p95 on dashboard
2) If kv entries rising and p95 > 1s -> cap continuous_batch.max_size to 16 via feature flag
3) Increase HPA minReplicas to 3 and set scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds to 180s
4) Monitor 5m; if stable, open rollback PR for change and schedule staged rollout
5) Notify CS with template: "We observed transient increased latency due to batching config; mitigation applied; monitoring continues."
```

maria: adding that to INC-2487 now.

kevin: monitoring logs, no new 504 spikes in last 2m.

dmitri: handing to kevin in 10. leaving notes in the incident ticket.

kevin: acknowledged — will follow up on PR and schedule canary for safer rollout.

lena (oncall): incident resolved for now. marking SEVERITY: mitigated. leaving channel for handoff. :white_check_mark:

site-bot: INCIDENT update saved to INC-2487, severity=mitigated, duration=00:46:32, responders=[lena, kevin, maria, omar, dmitri]
